page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top. Paragraphs numbered 2, 3 and 4 with short summary lines. Catchword in Greek at the lower right, below the last line.

main_text.p: 2. Forma externa promulgationis Le-gis. Quod fulgura crebra & ingens ignis conspiceretur, ac exaudirentur tonitrua, & fumaret mons Sinai, Cœli gloria eius operti, & laude eius terra repleta dicitur.

3. Finis istius tempestatis fuit, ut Legis-lator suis cultoribus reuerendum se esse demonstraret. Etsi enim paterni amoris argumentum erat, filijs praescribere regulam internarum & externarum actionum: tamen & auctoritatem suo numini sacro-sanctam esse voluit.
4. Locus, de quo in Exodo & alibi agitur.

De usu versiculi istius hoc tantum breuiter monebo, Ut olim veros Israelitas, gratis mentibus, cum caetera Dei beneficia, tum inprimis Legis promulgationem & repetitionem, veterisque Testamenti sanctionem, repetiuisse: & Deo, tantorum beneficiorum auctori, gratias egisse uidemus: ita nostrum esse, nunquam non Deo gratias agere, quod e tristi seruitute & tenebris regni Antichristiani liberatos, luce doctrinae Euangelicae illustrauit: quod in nobis quoq; fidei lucem accendit & fouet: quod alienos esse voluit ab omni

page.notes: Catchword at the lower right is in Greek and is only partly legible; the letters are not read. The paragraph ends mid-sentence at the foot of the page and continues on the next page. Long s is printed as a plain s throughout. Some letters, such as the f-like s in "Etsi", "Legis" and "sacrosanctam", are read as s. Short Greek catchword unreadable.
